text: Quality - Maintenance of water quality standards in and adjacent to areas of coal development on the Crow coal resource area will be required. Proposed mining and industrial development of coal resources must comply with all water quality standards set forth in the Federal Water Quality Acts. The State of Montana water quality standards under the State Water Pollution Control Act, must also be met. The section on Environmental Controls and Legislation in this chapter lists the exact citations. Methods used to maintain water quality standards might include monitoring, physical treatment, and chemical treatment. Regulatory agencies responsible for compliance within these standards are the Environmental Protection Agency, the Montana Department of State Lands, and the State Department of Health and Environmental Sciences. Surface Water - Effluent from a conversion plant may contribute to pollution of ponds, streams, or ground water. Such effluent would have to be monitored and treated if necessary to insure that undesirable physical characteristics or chemical constituents are not introduced into these waters. Evaporation or treatment ponds may have to be sealed to prevent percolation from reaching shallow ground-water supplies. Ponds would require adequate storage capacity to prevent accidental spills into surface water supplies. Provisions for safe disposal of solid wastes containing toxic materials must be made to prevent contamination of surface waters.
